## unblocked
Unblocked = institutional context behind code: PRs, design docs, chat, issues, incidents, code history, cross-repo code. Code search answers WHAT; Unblocked answers WHY, WHO, WHEN. Skipping risks duplicating rejected approaches, violating team conventions, stomping in-flight work, or missing incident context.

### Primary tool

`context_research` — semantic + relational research across docs, PRs, chat, issues, incidents, code. Use when question spans entities or needs synthesis. For a known URL, use `context_get_urls` instead — cheaper, returns fully hydrated content (supports GitHub/GitLab, Jira, Linear, Notion, Confluence, Slack, Google Docs, Asana, Coda, Sentry, Datadog, Stack Overflow Teams, Unblocked docs/threads).

### When to call context_research

Proactively. Do not wait for the user.

- Start of any planning, investigation, refactor, migration, or feature task. Fire in parallel with your first Explore/Grep/Read — zero latency cost.
- "Why does this exist" or "why done this way". Code cannot answer these.
- Behavior doesn't match the code. Check history first.
- Unfamiliar class, service, endpoint, flag, config key, or error string.
- Before writing new code. Check if the pattern, bug, fix, or helper already exists.
- Incident, alert, or outage. Connect affected systems to recent changes and fix patterns.
- Filtered activity lookups ("PRs merged last week in auth", "open incidents tagged ingestion").
- Before recommending a solution. Verify the approach hasn't been tried or rejected.

If unsure, call. Missed context is expensive.

### Effort

- `low` (default) — targeted lookup anchored on one entity, URL, or file.
- `medium` — exploratory, no clear anchor.
- `high` — planning, architecture, migration, incident retro, cross-system investigation. Use whenever producing a plan or design.

All Unblocked tools are read-only.
